threads.body: The new legacy tox factor installs the instrumentation package without its `[instruments]` extra, which can make this env drift from the other google-genai envs if additional instrument dependencies are ever added to that extra. Installing the package as `-e ...[instruments]` keeps the env aligned while still allowing the explicit `google-genai==2.8.0` pin.

This tox command omits `--vcr-record=none` even though the package’s test suite loads `pytest-vcr` via `pytest_plugins` in `tests/conftest.py`; adding the flag matches the other google-genai test envs and prevents accidental cassette recording if these tests start making HTTP calls in the future.
Why do we need to explicitly target this third version ? I'd rather not do this if we don't have to...

replies.body:
I think it's the same motivation as we (used to) have in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python-genai/pull/539 - test every major version we declare supported. Oldest tests v1, latest tests v3, nothing tests things in between, but we should.


Let's do it consistently via special requirement.v{major}.txt though as in the PR I linked

threads.body:
```suggestion
  test-instrumentation-google-genai-v2: pytest {toxinidir}/instrumentation/opentelemetry-instrumentation-google-genai/tests/interactions --vcr-record=none {posargs}
```

the goal is to catch all compatibility issues, not just this specific one
